claim: For an equal-weight unitary branch isometry V psi=K^(-1/2) sum_s W_s psi tensor |s>, the complementary-channel output purity on every pure input is exactly K^(-2)||M(psi tensor conjugate(psi))||_2^2, where M=sum_s W_s tensor conjugate(W_s).
interface: Finite-dimensional H=C^n; K unitaries W_s; complementary channels E(X)=K^(-1)sum_s W_s X W_s* and Phi(X)=K^(-1)[Tr(W_s X W_t*)]. Input is any unit vector psi.
evidence: Exact vectorization and Gram-matrix derivation in DERIVATION.txt. It also identifies the rank-one conjugate-product restriction and the identity/traceless decomposition.
costs: Symbolic finite-dimensional identity; no matrix is materialized. A full traceless 2-to-2 norm is a stronger sufficient condition than the required product-vector bound.
baseline: The filtered free-group construction uses a global purity estimate obtained from a coefficient-sphere penalty; this formula isolates the exact Veronese-cone norm that a lower-cost certificate must control.
falsifier: A mismatch in the isometry normalization, complement Gram entries, vectorization convention, or the equality Tr(S(rho)^2)=sum_{s,t}|<psi,W_s*W_t psi>|^2.
open_gate: No finite low-degree SOS or dimension-efficient product-vector certificate is derived. Independent specialist review remains open.

claim: For every Sidon set S of K Pauli labels in G=F2^(2q), K>=2, the exact Bell-output spectrum together with the max-nontrivial-Fourier purity upper bound cannot yield a positive two-copy von Neumann MOE additivity lower bound. For K>=3 this follows from f_K(N)>exp(-H_B/2) for every N=n^2>=1+binom(K,2); K=2 is separate and trivial.
interface: Uniform random-Pauli channel E_S on n=2^q dimensions, branch set S subset F2^(2q) of size K, with all unordered sums of distinct labels unique. Bell witness is the maximally entangled input to two copies. The certificate is S_min(E_S)>=-ln(1/n+(1-1/n)beta^2), beta=max_nontrivial |F(chi)|/K.
evidence: The Sidon Bell spectrum, additive energy 3K^2-2K, Fourier moment lower bound, monotonicity/endpoint analysis, and exact strict endpoint comparisons are derived in DERIVATION.txt. Endpoint inequalities reduce to 18sqrt(2)<29 and 128sqrt(2)<261. Numerical fixture checks are in evidence/verify_product_vector_pauli.py.
costs: All-K proof is O(1) symbolic algebra; the finite checker enumerates 64 characters and 64^2 pairs for GF(8). No channel matrices or global state optimization are generated.
baseline: The source-reported free-group constructions use a uniform all-input purity certificate and exact Bell quotient, with filtering/high-girth finite transfer. This result rules out only the stated Pauli/Sidon max-Fourier certificate route.
falsifier: An error in the Pauli purity identity, Sidon multiplicities, additive-energy Fourier moments, derivative endpoint argument, or exact comparisons. The finite checker alone does not validate the analytic proof.
open_gate: This is not a no-go for Pauli channels or for tighter purity/entropy certificates, non-Sidon sets, non-Pauli branch families, or different witnesses. No MOE violation or nonviolation is established for the actual channels in general.

claim: The Gold graph S={(x,x^3):x in GF(8)} is a Sidon set in F2^6 with maximum nontrivial Walsh magnitude 4; its Bell probabilities are 1/8 once and 1/32 twenty-eight times, and the max-Fourier purity certificate is 11/32.
interface: GF(8)=F2[z]/(z^3+z+1); K=n=8, N=64. Use the Hermitian Pauli labels indexed by F2^6 and the standard symplectic character pairing.
evidence: Exact integer-field enumeration and rational pair-count checks in evidence/verify_product_vector_pauli.py. The file reports Bell entropy 3.2924491077 nats, one-copy entropy lower bound 1.0678406300 nats, and purity-certificate gap lower bound -1.1567678477 nats.
costs: Under 4096 field/pair operations; negligible time and memory. No matrix construction or entropy minimization is performed.
baseline: Compared with the general Sidon/Fourier lower bound, the fixture attains R_8(64)=16 exactly and has beta^2=1/4.
falsifier: A wrong GF(8) multiplication polynomial, trace, Walsh sign, or ordered-pair multiplicity; the script assertions would fail for the encoded fixture.
open_gate: Finite enumeration is not a proof of the all-K theorem, does not calculate the actual channel MOE, and supplies no positive gap.

claim: As of 2026-10-08, arXiv:2609.18747v1 reports a near-one-bit Bell-witness MOE additivity violation simultaneously for all Renyi orders with output dimension O(epsilon^-3), and arXiv:2610.06533v1 reports an explicit finite von Neumann example with 8 output qubits, 37,608,898 input qubits, and gap greater than 1/1024 nats.
interface: The first source uses equal-weight mixed-orthogonal branches from direct products of free groups; its non-random corollary is an existence sequence from strong convergence. The second source states a closed-form real-algebraic finite channel at p=1.
evidence: Primary sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.18747v1, Sections 2, 4-7; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06533v1, Corollary 2.2 and Sections 4-6. The source proof mechanisms were read selectively, not independently validated end-to-end.
costs: For 2609.18747 the non-random existence corollary provides no closed-form matrices or producing algorithm; the finite high-probability Haar-orthogonal example uses output dimension 320. For 2610.06533 the reported channel input is 37,608,898 qubits and output is 8 qubits; no huge matrices are materialized here.
baseline: These are the strongest current primary-source baselines found for near-one-bit all-order and compact-output von Neumann constructions, respectively.
falsifier: A defect in the source constructions or their imported strong-convergence, free-group, or high-girth lemmas; no full independent proof audit is supplied here.
open_gate: Complete proof correctness, independent replay, and novelty/priority remain UNKNOWN. These are source claims, not external validation.
